newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso says CVRD sale to go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso says CVRD sale to go ahead.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said Sunday that the government would not reschedule the April 29 auction of mining conglomerate Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD).
"We are not going to change the date of the auction," Cardoso told reporters in Rio de Janeiro.
The Brazilian president said government lawyers were working on an appeal against an injunction granted against the sell-off by a Sao Paulo judge on Friday.
The injunction has suspended, at least for now, the scheduled sale of a controlling 45 percent of voting shares, due to go on the auction block at 1000 local/1300 GMT Tuesday.
There are also other court cases that could yet hamper the sale though the government maintains any delay would only be for a few days.
Cardoso defended the controversial privatization of the world's largest iron ore exporter. He said it had been amply discussed in Congress and by the public at large.
Police in Rio plan to beef up security around the stock exchange where the auction will take place.

On Sunday outside the Copacabana Palace Hotel in Rio where Cardoso held a meeting with Argentine President Carlos Menem, some 200 leftist demonstrators protesting against the auction and against the government clashed with police.
At least one tear gas grenade was fired into the crowd and eyewitnesses said at least two people were arrested.
